items.title: NATS Server allows unauthenticated memory exhaustion through incomplete MQTT CONNECT packets
items.description:
Background

NATS.io is a high performance open source pub-sub distributed communication technology, built for the cloud, on-premise, IoT and edge computing.

The NATS Server supports MQTT clients, including authentication and parsing of MQTT CONNECT packets.

Problem Description

An unauthenticated MQTT client could cause the server to retain large incomplete MQTT CONNECT packets before authentication completed.

The parser retained partial pre-authentication packet data while waiting for the advertised MQTT packet length to be completed. An attacker could therefore consume server memory until authentication timeouts closed the connections.

Affected Versions

Versions v2.14.2, v2.12.11 and below are vulnerable. The issue is fixed in v2.14.3 and v2.12.12.

Workarounds

iocs.response_guidance: Block via DNS RPZ or Secure DNS. Search proxy logs. Submit to threat intel sharing platform.
iocs.detection_guidance: Monitor DNS query logs, proxy logs, and certificate transparency logs for domain resolution.

items.title: CodeWhale: exec_shell parallel-readonly classifier auto-approves fd/rg/git grep exec flags enabling silent RCE
items.description:
Maintainer resolution

The CodeWhale maintainers validated this report. CodeWhale 0.8.67 and earlier are affected. Version 0.9.0 contains the fix in commit 208421b9d23d81cea3311a1eeb2a2ea81d637686. Users should upgrade to 0.9.0 or later. The original reporter analysis is preserved below.

Summary
The interactive Agent profile of DeepSeek-TUI (CodeWhale) is explicitly documented to gate every shell command behind an approval prompt (config.rs:3725-3736). However, ExecShellTool::approval_requirement_for(&tool_input) downgrades the requirement from Required to Auto for any command the classifier deems "parallel read-only" (shell.rs:2314-2320). registered_tool_approval_required returns false for Auto before the auto_approve check runs (turn_loop.rs:37-38), so no pr

// SENTINEL APEX — CVE-2026-83816 Remote Code Execution Detection
// Product: Web Application | Generated: 2026-11-20T05:47:09Z
// Deploy to: Microsoft Sentinel / Defender XDR
let lookback = 1d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe", "httpd.exe", "nginx.exe", "tomcat.exe", "java.exe")
    and FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "bash", "sh", "python.exe", "python3"))

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("update", "install", "backup", "deploy"))  // filter known-good

items.description:
Resolution

- Affected versions: < 3.3.4
- First patched version: 3.3.4

The reported payload was reproduced against the 3.3.3 release tag and verified to scale approximately linearly against the 3.3.4 release tag.

Original report

The following report describes the issue before the fix.

Summary
mistune's inline image parsing reaches precedence_scan for ![ openers because the two guards that keep the link path linear are both gated behind not is_image. A small default-renderer document of the form "![" * N + "x" + "]" * N produces O(N²) CPU with no plugins.

Root Cause
For ![ openers, is_image is True, so both linearizing guards are skipped

items.title: NLTK: StreamBackedCorpusView constructor os.stat leaks out-of-root file existence, size, and mtime bypassing pathsec ENFORCE
items.description:
Summary

StreamBackedCorpusView, a public API in nltk/corpus/reader/util.py, applies the pathsec sandbox to the file content it reads but not to the file metadata it probes in its constructor. When the view is created with a plain string fileid, __init__ calls os.stat(self._fileid).st_size with no pathsec validation, so an application that passes an attacker influenced path to the constructor discloses whether an arbitrary out of root file exists and, if it does, its exact byte size and modification time, even when nltk.pathsec.ENFORCE is True. This is the residual metadata channel left open by the fix for CVE-2026-63312 (GHSA-x5ph-mj9p-rfr8), which closed arbitrary content read on the same code path but did not bring the sibling os.stat under the sandbox.

items.title: OliveTin: Second-Order OS Command Injection via shellAfterCompleted
items.description:
Summary

OliveTin's shellAfterCompleted post-execution hook injects unsanitized variables — including arbitrary command output (output), the authenticated username (ot_username), and the exit code (exitCode) — directly into a shell command template processed by sh -c. Unlike the main action's argument handling, no checkShellArgumentSafety validation is applied to these variables. An attacker who can influence the output of a command (e.g., via user-supplied arguments that reflect in stdout, or through trusted-header username spoofing) can inject arbitrary OS commands into the post-execution shell.
